claims.statement: For every input law on the governed half-skew BSSC product channel P^{otimes 2}, let c_in=P(X_1X_2=11)-Pr[X_1=1]Pr[X_2=1] and C_out=I(Y_1;Y_2)+I(Z_1;Z_2). A paired-receiver binary-table curvature argument proves the unconditional inequality C_out >= 31 c_in^2/(20 ln 2). Canonical transaction 9bb22afe5abd3e1d9f419c1717bd61bb33a958ff supplies the necessary inequality C_out < 7/160 for any finite two-letter Marton law whose unnormalized value exceeds twice the optimal one-letter randomized-time-division value. Consequently every such gain forces |c_in| < sqrt(7 ln 2/248) < 7/50. This is a necessary condition only; it does not construct a Marton gain, rule one out, tensorize Marton's functional, or give a capacity converse.

program/multiletter-marton-achievability.title: Multiletter Marton achievability
program/multiletter-marton-achievability.objective: Determine whether finite-letter Marton coding can improve half-skew BSSC achievable sum rates and rigorously characterize structural restrictions on candidate multiletter witnesses.

program/multiletter-marton-achievability.title: Two-letter marginal and correlation pruning
program/multiletter-marton-achievability.summary: Develop necessary marginal-balance, output-decorrelation, input-covariance, and symmetry-family restrictions on candidate two-letter Marton improvements.
conditions: Requires the accepted two-letter Marton-to-input bounds in transaction 33a5944dca980bf94cc869c6c7dee2d04385ff58.
Requires the accepted exact directed randomized-time-division threshold in transaction 88a1004f309460f3ec1cacdae88d30f88559f9bc.

item/marton-multiletter-finite-foundatio.title: Finite-super-symbol, superadditivity, and RTD calculus proof
item/marton-multiletter-finite-foundatio.summary: Proof used to establish the linked accepted claim. It bounds each finite-auxiliary Marton functional by binary output entropies, concatenates independent finite laws using the minimum-term inequality to prove superadditivity, applies Fekete's lemma, and proves exact scaling for repeated selected laws. Under (H-Marton), it converts an epsilon-optimal finite law into a finite super-channel Marton rate pair and flattens the resulting code to the original channel. Separately, receiver-skew symmetrization reduces randomized time division to a scalar difference curve, whose derivative identifies q_-=(15-sqrt(105))/30 and yields the accepted closed form. The proof preserves all stated conditional hypotheses and does not establish a fixed-blocklength capacity converse.

item/marton-multiletter-finite-foundatio.title: Finite-auxiliary Marton multiletter foundation and directed RTD threshold
item/marton-multiletter-finite-foundatio.summary:
Accepted statement:

For the governed half-skew BSSC P and every n >= 1, define M_n^fin(P) as the supremum of the displayed private-message Marton functional over finite auxiliary alphabets U,V,W and finite laws (U,V,W)-X^n-(Y^n,Z^n). Unconditionally, 0 <= M_n^fin(P) <= 2n, M_{m+n}^fin(P) >= M_m^fin(P)+M_n^fin(P), and Fekete's lemma gives lim_n M_n^fin(P)/n = sup_n M_n^fin(P)/n; k independent copies of a selected n-letter law of value S_n have value exactly k S_n. Assume (H-Marton), the exact finite-DMBC private-message Marton achievability theorem stated in the README. Then C_sum(P) >= M_n^fin(P)/n for every n and hence C_sum(P) is at least the displayed Fekete limit. For the exact BSSC randomized-time-division value L_RTD, the README's symmetrization and calculus proof gives the stated closed form at q_-=(15-sqrt(105))/30, and the directed standard-library certificate proves the strict intervals 0.3616428844219546156634415781505870072079810107238605552037137298028007 < L_RTD < 0.3616428844219546156634415781505870072079810107238605552037137298028008 and 0.7232857688439092313268831563011740144159620214477211104074274596056014 < 2 L_RTD < 0.7232857688439092313268831563011740144159620214477211104074274596056016. Assume additionally (H-binary), the exact binary-input Marton-equals-randomized-time-division theorem stated in the README; then M_1^fin(P)=L_RTD. Under (H-Marton), a selected finite n-letter law strictly improves the governed RTD achievable lower bound through super-symbol normalization iff S_n > n L_RTD; under both hypotheses this is equivalently a strict improvement over the complete one-letter Marton sum optimum. This append-only claim repairs only the finite-auxiliary scope, conditional super-symbol conclusion, conditional one-letter identification, and decimal certification of transaction f6ea30479b9ca461294ba89a8a1a31c06ce59d08; that transaction is a corrective/provenance reference rather than a mathematical premise. No fixed-n equality is a capacity converse.

Scope qualifications (verbatim):
- The capacity lower bound C_sum(P) >= M_n^fin(P)/n and the resulting Fekete-limit lower bound are conditional on (H-Marton).
- The identity M_1^fin(P)=L_RTD is conditional on (H-binary).
- Equivalence between improvement over RTD and improvement over the complete one-letter Marton optimum requires both (H-Marton) and (H-binary).
- All optimizations defining M_n^fin(P) are restricted to finite auxiliary alphabets; no optimizer or cardinality theorem is assumed.
- No fixed-n equality is asserted or used as a capacity converse.
- The declared transaction is corrective/provenance material only and is not a mathematical dependency.

item/marton-rtd-directed-interval-certif.title: Directed RTD threshold interval certificate
item/marton-rtd-directed-interval-certif.summary: Computation used for the certified numerical portion of the linked accepted claim. It brackets sqrt(105) by exact rational square comparisons, propagates directed 120-digit decimal intervals through the accepted closed form for L_RTD, expands correctly rounded logarithms outward, and verifies that the resulting enclosures lie strictly inside the stated intervals for L_RTD and 2L_RTD. It certifies only those intervals and the associated finite-scope structural audit; it does not prove (H-Marton), (H-binary), or any capacity converse.

item/two-letter-marton-full-support-nece.title: Full-support and mass-floor necessity for a two-letter Marton gain
item/two-letter-marton-full-support-nece.summary:
Accepted statement:

For the half-skew BSSC product channel P^{otimes 2}, every finite Marton law whose induced super-input X_1X_2 is supported on at most three of {00,01,10,11} has unnormalized Marton sum value strictly below 0.695 bits. A fair one-letter randomized-time-division schedule with reflected rational conditional priors 1/6 and 5/6, repeated independently twice, has exact unnormalized value B_{1/6}=2h_2(1/4)+h_2(1/12)-h_2(5/12)-1/3>0.7231 bits. Therefore every strict two-letter Marton improvement over twice the optimal one-letter randomized-time-division value must assign positive mass to all four super-input symbols. Quantitatively, every such improving witness must assign mass greater than 1/180 to each of 00 and 11 and mass greater than 1/325 to each of 01 and 10. This is a support-pruning theorem for the two-letter Marton functional, not a full-support no-gain theorem or an unrestricted capacity converse.

Scope qualifications (verbatim):
- The result concerns the unnormalized two-letter Marton functional for the half-skew BSSC product channel.
- It is a support-pruning theorem only; it does not prove that full-support Marton laws cannot yield a gain.
- It is not a converse for unrestricted broadcast coding or a determination of unrestricted sum capacity.
- The numerical attestation supports the finite algebraic and numerical inequalities, while the universal Marton reduction and calculus steps are established in the written proof.

item/two-letter-marton-marginal-correlat.title: Directed marginal and output-correlation pruning audit
item/two-letter-marton-marginal-correlat.summary: Tool used for the computationally audited portion of the linked accepted claim. Using exact rational checks and outward-rounded standard-library decimal intervals, it reconstructs the required directed RTD threshold and verifies the coordinate, correlation, covariance, sum-marginal, and reflected-family endpoint comparisons supporting the accepted rational cutoffs. It does not replace the analytic information-theoretic identities, concavity arguments, or Pinsker derivation and does not establish a gain, a no-gain theorem, or a capacity converse.

item/two-letter-marton-marginal-correlat.title: Output-correlation decomposition and concave-envelope pruning proof
item/two-letter-marton-marginal-correlat.summary: Proof used to establish the linked accepted claim. It combines the required Marton-to-input rows with the exact decomposition of the averaged product-channel input mutual information into two coordinate terms minus one half of the within-receiver output correlation. Coordinatewise and sum-marginal concave envelopes, together with the required directed threshold, give the accepted marginal restrictions and output-correlation bound. The affine BSSC output laws and a Pinsker argument give the accepted input-covariance bound, while monotonicity on the reflected/transposed one-parameter family gives the stated alpha window. This proof item establishes only the necessary conditions in the linked claim.

item/two-letter-marton-marginal-correlat.title: Marginal-balance and correlation necessities for a two-letter Marton gain
item/two-letter-marton-marginal-correlat.summary:
Accepted statement:

For the governed half-skew BSSC product channel P^{otimes 2}, let M be the unnormalized finite-auxiliary Marton sum value of any law (W,U,V)-X_1X_2-(Y^2,Z^2), let q_i=Pr[X_i=1], Q=q_1+q_2, let C_out=I(Y_1;Y_2)+I(Z_1;Z_2), and let c_in=P(X_1X_2=11)-q_1q_2. Canonical transaction 33a5944dca980bf94cc869c6c7dee2d04385ff58 supplies the two pre-averaging Marton-to-input rows and their universal average M <= G(P_{X_1X_2})+2r, while canonical transaction 88a1004f309460f3ec1cacdae88d30f88559f9bc supplies the exact directed threshold T=2L_RTD. The exact identity G=F(q_1)+F(q_2)-C_out/2 and the coordinatewise concave row envelopes imply that M>T forces q_1,q_2 in (3/8,5/8), hence in (7/20,13/20), together with 17/20<Q<23/20, C_out<7/160=0.04375<0.044 bits, and |c_in|<7/40. On the reflected/transposed family P(00)=P(11)=alpha and P(01)=P(10)=1/2-alpha, a gain additionally forces 1/8<alpha<5/13. These are necessary conditions only; they do not establish a two-letter gain, rule one out, or give a capacity converse.

Scope qualifications (verbatim):
- Applies to the governed half-skew BSSC product channel P^{otimes 2}.
- Applies to the unnormalized finite-auxiliary Marton sum value.
- The conclusions are necessary conditions conditional on M>T.
- It neither constructs nor proves a two-letter gain.
- It does not rule out a two-letter gain.
- It is not a capacity converse.
- From the threshold reference, only the unconditional RTD calculus and interval certificate are needed; neither (H-Marton) nor (H-binary) is used.
